whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should pursue the Technical Architect credential?

personas.label: Experienced Salesforce architects
personas.description: You lead complex implementations and want to pursue the highest Salesforce architecture credential.

personas.label: Consulting practice leaders
personas.description: You design solutions across Salesforce products and explain those choices to enterprise clients.

personas.label: Architect credential holders
personas.description: You hold Application Architect and System Architect and are considering the CTA assessment.

examDifficulty.heading: How difficult is the Technical Architect assessment?
examDifficulty.summary: Technical Architect is Salesforce’s most advanced credential and requires a two-stage assessment rather than a multiple-choice exam. First earn Application Architect and System Architect. Then pass a readiness evaluation and present and defend a design to a review board.
bullets: No multiple-choice paper. Design a solution for a scenario and defend your decisions.
Two prerequisites. Application Architect and System Architect require eight exam passes across the two paths, with Platform Developer I counting for both, so there are seven distinct exams.
Two assessment stages. Complete the architect evaluation before the review board.
Significant fees. The Architect Evaluation is $1,500 (retake $750) and the Architect Review Board is $4,500 (retake $2,250): $6,000 in total, plus taxes.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Candidates often bring experience leading large Salesforce programs and spend months rehearsing the format with mock boards. Preparation means practising the presentation and defence, not only studying documentation.

examFormat.heading: How the Technical Architect assessment works
examFormat.intro: There is no multiple-choice CTA exam. The credential uses two scenario-based stages:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Both stages use a hypothetical enterprise with existing systems, business goals, constraints, and problems. You design a solution, present it, and explain your decisions.
bestWayToPass: Complete both prerequisites: Application Architect and System Architect must be active before applying.
Practise your defence: Rehearse with people who will question and challenge your choices.
Address the stated need: A sophisticated design still fails if it misses the scenario requirements.
Justify each component: Explain why it is included and what alternative you considered.

certificationCard.description: Technical Architect is Salesforce's top credential. It is awarded through a two-stage assessment rather than a multiple-choice exam: a readiness evaluation, then a review board where you present and defend an architecture for a hypothetical enterprise scenario.

keyConcepts.h2: Technical Architect (CTA): credential and assessment guide

blocks.heading: Credential requirements
blocks.body: CTA follows two role-based credentials. Application Architect requires Platform App Builder, Platform Developer I, Data Architect, and Sharing and Visibility Architect. System Architect requires Platform Developer I, Integration Architect, Identity and Access Management Architect, and Development Lifecycle and Deployment Architect. Platform Developer I counts for both, so the two paths include seven distinct exams. After earning both credentials, complete two separately booked and paid assessment stages.

blocks.heading: First stage: architect evaluation
blocks.body: The evaluation is a readiness assessment with a Salesforce evaluator. You work through a scenario, create a design, and discuss it. Passing opens access to the review board. Treat this as a real assessment: understanding the requirements and justifying choices are also central to the board.

blocks.heading: Final stage: review board
blocks.body: For the review board, you receive an enterprise scenario, design a solution, and present it to a panel of CTAs. The panel asks detailed questions about the design. Judges assess whether you understood the requirements, can justify decisions and risks, and can respond to a challenge. Their decision is based on required areas, not a percentage score.

blocks.heading: What the judges assess
blocks.body: The same skills appear across both stages: cover every stated requirement; explain important choices and alternatives; recognize trade-offs; identify risks and mitigations; and communicate clearly to a business audience. Deep platform knowledge is expected. The assessment focuses on the reasoning built on that knowledge.

blocks.heading: Prepare through practice
blocks.body: Use complete scenarios, create a design within a time limit, and present it to people who will interrupt with questions. Follow a consistent outline covering data, security, integration, delivery lifecycle, and licensing. Record yourself and notice where you avoid a clear decision. Mock boards with practising CTAs help prepare for the actual format.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the Salesforce Technical Architect assessment
scenarioTips.intro: Preparation is about applying architecture knowledge and explaining decisions under pressure. Practise these skills with full scenarios.

blocks.heading: Explain each decision
blocks.body: For every component, state the requirement it serves and the alternative you considered.

blocks.heading: Discuss trade-offs
blocks.body: Name the cost or limitation of each design choice and why you accepted it.

blocks.heading: Plan for risk
blocks.body: Consider data volume, integration outages, adoption, and governance, then explain how you would mitigate issues.

blocks.heading: Connect to business outcomes
blocks.body: Start with what the solution achieves, then explain the design in language stakeholders can follow.

blocks.heading: Rehearse aloud
blocks.body: Practise mock boards with people who interrupt and challenge your reasoning; reading alone cannot build this skill.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Architect Certifications
nextCertsAfter.intro: The two credentials you need before CTA:

sampleQuestions.question: Which two credentials are required before beginning the CTA assessment?
options: Administrator and Advanced Administrator
Sales Cloud Consultant and Service Cloud Consultant
Application Architect and System Architect
Platform Developer II and JavaScript Developer I
sampleQuestions.explanation: Candidates must hold both role-based architect credentials. Together, their requirements cover seven distinct exams.
whyWrong: Administrator credentials do not qualify a candidate for CTA.
Consultant credentials belong to a different path.
These developer credentials are not the two CTA prerequisites.

sampleQuestions.question: How is the CTA credential assessed?
options: Design a scenario solution and defend it live
Complete Trailhead superbadges without an assessment
Submit a portfolio of past client implementations
Pass a 60-question multiple-choice exam
sampleQuestions.explanation: CTA uses scenario design and a live defence rather than a multiple-choice exam.
whyWrong: Superbadges are not the CTA assessment.
Candidates solve a supplied scenario rather than submit only past work.
CTA has no multiple-choice exam.

sampleQuestions.question: A candidate’s design is elegant but leaves two stated business needs unanswered. What is the likely result?
options: Pass because the technical design is strong
Receive a request for a written follow-up
Have the judges revise the scenario
Missed requirements lead to a failing design
sampleQuestions.explanation: The design must answer the scenario. Missing requirements is a common reason candidates do not pass.
whyWrong: Technical quality does not make up for missing the brief.
There is no written follow-up that replaces required coverage.
The candidate must work with the supplied scenario.

sampleQuestions.question: Before Salesforce allows a candidate to schedule the final architecture review board, what does the earlier Evaluation check?
options: Check readiness before allowing access to the review board
Award the CTA credential directly
Replace Application Architect for experienced candidates
Test Apex coding ability
sampleQuestions.explanation: The checkpoint confirms the candidate is prepared for the board review. It is a prerequisite to booking, not a substitute for either architect credential.
whyWrong: The CTA credential is awarded after the board.
It does not replace either prerequisite credential.
The evaluation tests architecture reasoning, not Apex coding.

sampleQuestions.question: A judge questions a candidate’s choice to use middleware. What is the strongest response?
options: Call it an industry best practice
Say the client requested it
Explain why the middleware fits and its trade-off
Replace it immediately with a direct connection
sampleQuestions.explanation: The panel wants to hear the reasoning for the choice, the alternative, and the cost or trade-off accepted.
whyWrong: A general claim does not show why it fits this scenario.
An unexplained client request is not architectural reasoning.
Changing a design without evaluating the objection suggests the original choice was not reasoned.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the CTA panel assess?
options: Slide design and visual polish
Architecture judgement and communication
How quickly the candidate types
Memorized feature names and limits
sampleQuestions.explanation: Platform knowledge is assumed. The assessment focuses on applying that knowledge through sound decisions and clear explanation.
whyWrong: Readable visuals help but are not the main criterion.
There is no typing task.
Prerequisite exams assess platform knowledge; the board assesses architecture judgement.

sampleQuestions.question: How many distinct exams are needed across both prerequisite credentials?
options: Seven distinct exams
Eight, because the paths have no exams in common
Four, one for each architect area
Two, one for each credential
sampleQuestions.explanation: Each credential has four exams, and Platform Developer I appears in both. That makes seven distinct exams.
whyWrong: The two paths share Platform Developer I.
Four exams cover only one of the two credentials.
Each credential requires four exams, not one.

sampleQuestions.question: A candidate explains a design clearly to architects but loses the business stakeholders. Why does this matter?
options: Only the evaluation stage considers communication
It changes the fee but not the result
It does not matter because the judges are technical
Explain the design to business stakeholders
sampleQuestions.explanation: Judges consider whether stakeholders who fund and use the solution can understand it.
whyWrong: Communication matters in both assessment stages.
Fees do not depend on presentation quality.
The panel still assesses communication even though its members are architects.

sampleQuestions.question: Which preparation best reflects the CTA assessment format?
options: Watch presentations without practising one
Practise mock boards with live challenges
Memorize governor limits only
Read prerequisite exam guides again
sampleQuestions.explanation: Live practice helps candidates learn to explain and defend an architecture under questioning.
whyWrong: Watching alone does not practise the defence.
Platform limits are useful knowledge but not the main skill being assessed.
Those guides focus on prerequisite exams, not this assessment format.

sampleQuestions.question: What do the two CTA stages cost in total, according to the Salesforce pricing page?
options: The price of one standard US$200 exam
US$6,000 total
A fixed annual subscription
No extra fee beyond the prerequisites
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce lists the Architect Evaluation at $1,500 (retake $750) and the Architect Review Board at $4,500 (retake $2,250), which is $6,000 for a first-time pass of both, before taxes.
whyWrong: The combined stages cost more than a standard exam.
The stages are assessment fees, not an annual subscription.
The prerequisites do not include the assessment fees.

sampleQuestions.question: A candidate says the design has no risks because every requirement is met. How might the panel respond?
options: Favorably if the architecture diagram is detailed
Trade-offs and risks are part of the assessment
Treat confidence as the main success measure
Ignore risk because it is scored separately
sampleQuestions.explanation: A design always involves trade-offs. Naming risks and mitigations shows the candidate has analysed it.
whyWrong: Diagram detail does not replace risk analysis.
Confidence alone is not the assessment criterion.
Risk is part of the overall judgement.

sampleQuestions.question: What kind of scenario is used for the review board?
options: A production org the candidate must configure
The candidate’s own past project
A hypothetical enterprise with constraints
A set of multiple-choice scenario questions
sampleQuestions.explanation: Candidates design for a hypothetical enterprise described in the scenario.
whyWrong: The board does not require live configuration.
Past work is not the assessment scenario.
The board is a presentation and defence, not multiple choice.

sampleQuestions.question: Why use a repeatable outline when presenting?
options: It guarantees a pass regardless of the design
It replaces the need for an architecture diagram
It removes the panel’s question period
Use custom work only when standard features fall short
sampleQuestions.explanation: A consistent order helps candidates address data, security, integration, lifecycle, and licensing.
whyWrong: Structure supports preparation but does not guarantee an outcome.
Diagrams remain useful to explain architecture.
The panel asks questions after the presentation.

sampleQuestions.question: Which exam counts toward both Application Architect and System Architect?
options: Data Architect
Integration Architect
Platform Developer I
Sharing and Visibility Architect
sampleQuestions.explanation: Platform Developer I is required for both credentials, leaving seven distinct exams across the two paths.
whyWrong: Data Architect applies to Application Architect only.
Integration Architect applies to System Architect only.
Sharing and Visibility Architect applies to Application Architect only.

sampleQuestions.question: What can a candidate usually do after not passing the review board?
options: Prepare and attempt the board again
Receive a lower credential automatically
Retake all seven prerequisite exams
Never pursue CTA again
sampleQuestions.explanation: Candidates may prepare and reattempt; fees apply to each attempt. Check current retake pricing with Salesforce.
whyWrong: There is no automatic alternate credential.
Active prerequisite credentials do not need to be retaken.
A failed attempt does not permanently prevent a later attempt.

expertInsight: You cannot prepare for CTA by reading alone. The panel looks at how you choose between reasonable designs, explain the business need behind each choice, and respond to challenges. Some candidates know Salesforce well but miss requirements or cannot defend their decisions. Practise presenting aloud with people who will interrupt and question the design.
